summary.text: Orbital hybridisation is the mixing of atomic orbitals into new hybrid orbitals, with different energies and shapes, suited to pairing electrons into chemical bonds in valence bond theory.
In a carbon atom with four single bonds, one s orbital and three p orbitals combine into four equivalent sp³ mixtures arranged in a tetrahedron.
Linus Pauling developed the theory in 1931 to explain simple molecules such as methane, and it is now an effective heuristic for the structures of organic compounds.

items.prompt: Taking carbon's s and p orbitals as they are, one would expect three bonds at right angles and a weaker fourth. What does methane actually show?

options.label: Two strong bonds and two very weak ones
Four bonds of equivalent strength
Three strong bonds and one weaker one
Four bonds, with the one from the s orbital strongest

items.explain: Methane has four C–H bonds of equivalent strength, which Pauling explained with four equivalent hybrid orbitals.

items.prompt: Why do the carbons in ethylene hybridise as sp² rather than sp³?

options.label: They need one pi bond for the double bond and form only three sigma bonds
They need four sigma bonds, so they use every orbital
Their s orbital is too weak to mix with more than one p orbital
The hydrogen atoms force each carbon into a triangle

items.explain: One pi bond is required for the double bond and only three sigma bonds form per carbon, so the 2s orbital mixes with just two of the three 2p orbitals.

items.prompt: A carbon atom promotes an electron from its 2s orbital to an empty 2p orbital, which costs energy, before bonding four hydrogens. Why is that worthwhile?

options.label: The promotion itself releases energy
Hydrogen atoms supply the energy that it costs
Two extra bonds release more energy than the promotion costs
The electron is no longer needed afterwards

items.explain: The energy released by forming two additional bonds more than compensates for the excitation energy, favouring four C–H bonds.

items.prompt: Why would carbon mix its s and p orbitals, rather than use them separately, to bond four hydrogens in methane?

options.label: Separate orbitals cannot overlap with hydrogen at all
Mixing makes the core orbitals join in the bonding
Mixing adds extra electrons to the carbon atom
Four equal bonds give the lowest energy and need equal orbitals

items.explain: Quantum mechanics gives the lowest energy when the four bonds are equivalent, which requires equivalent orbitals; these are the four sp³ hybrids.

items.prompt: What can chemists predict reliably from the amount of s or p character in an atom's orbitals?

options.label: The melting point of any solid
The acidity or basicity of a molecule
The number of neutrons in the nucleus
The colour of any compound

items.explain: The amount of p or s character, decided mainly by hybridisation, can reliably predict molecular properties such as acidity or basicity.

items.prompt: In ethylene, each carbon mixes its 2s orbital with only two of its three 2p orbitals. What becomes of the third 2p orbital?

options.label: It joins the mix as a fourth hybrid orbital
It is lost, so the carbon forms fewer bonds
It merges with the 1s orbital of a hydrogen
It stays unhybridised, as a plain p orbital

items.explain: In sp² hybridisation the third 2p orbital remains unhybridised, giving three sp² orbitals and one remaining p orbital.
